records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public groups#members endpoint accepts a completely unvalidated params[:limit] with no upper bound, so any logged-in user can pass limit=10000000 and have the full member list of any visible group serialized in one response. An anonymous/authenticated user enumerates every username, avatar URL, and last_seen timestamp of any visible (including large automatic) group in a single request, enabling bulk user-enumeration scraping that the previous 200-hard-cap-for-automatic-groups behavior throttled, and a large limit on a huge group (e.g. trust_level groups) causes a heavy DB query and serialization spike per request — a cheap DoS amplification vector.
records.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the diff sets `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and uses it directly in `group.users.order(:username_lower).limit(limit).offset(offset)` with no upper bound or validation. Previously, the code applied a hard cap for automatic groups (`limit = (params[:limit] || 200).to_i` and only paginated for automatic groups), which throttled large automatic groups. With the new behavior, any requester who can access the endpoint can pass an arbitrarily large `limit` and trigger large DB + serialization work and bulk member enumeration in a single response.

records.rationale: In `Admin::GroupsController#add_members`, the code iterates `usernames.split(",")` and only adds when `User.find_by_username(username)` returns a user; non-matching usernames are silently ignored (no else/error/feedback). It then renders `success_json` as long as `group.save` succeeds, even if zero users were added (`add_members` action in diff). This matches the finding that a typo/deleted username is dropped while the API still returns 200 success, and the diff also removes the prior spec coverage for silently skipping non-existent users.
